result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
I approved one of the two pending work orders on Transformer 1 and left the other pending. Nothing was cancelled and no priorities changed.

**Pending-approval work orders (both status WAPPR)**

| WO | Description | Priority | Reported | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection - Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04 UTC | none |
| 1000052 | Transformer 1 - oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check for T2 thermal fault | 3 | 2026-09-30 23:15 UTC | FC006 (overheating) |

**Latest oil sample (2024-01-19, about 2.7 years old)**
- Hydrogen 2850 ppm, methane 7400 ppm, ethane 5470 ppm, ethylene 16650 ppm, acetylene 7 ppm. All five fault gases are present.
- CO 32 ppm and CO2 1340 ppm.

**Fault classification**
The dissolved gas analysis tool failed twice ("LLM unavailable"), so I worked out the IEC 60599 ratios by hand:
- Acetylene/ethylene = 0.0004, which is below 0.1.
- Methane/hydrogen = 2.60, which is above 1.
- Ethylene/ethane = 3.04, which falls in the 1–4 band.
- **Result: T2 thermal fault (300–700 °C).** The ratios don't point to arcing or discharge.
- **Paper:** probably not involved. CO is low at 32 ppm and the CO2/CO ratio is about 42.

**What I did**
- **1000052 – Approved.** It is an oil sampling job and it targets the T2 thermal fault the gases show. It isn't arcing or tap changer work, so its priority stays at 3.
- **1000051 – Left pending.** The gases show a main-tank thermal fault with no arcing signature (acetylene/ethylene is only 0.0004), so they don't support a tap-changer fault. It also has no failure code and its target start date (2024-01-19) is out of date.
- **Cancellations:** none. There are only two work orders on Transformer 1 and they cover different jobs.

| WO | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1000052 | Approved (priority stays 3) | DGA = T2 thermal (0.0004 / 2.60 / 3.04); description matches this fault and it is an oil sampling job; FC006 overheating fits; CO 32 ppm, so paper probably not involved; not arcing or tap changer work, so no priority change |
| 1000051 | Left pending (priority stays 1, unchanged) | Tap changer inspection, but the gases indicate a main-tank T2 thermal fault with no arcing (acetylene 7 ppm, acetylene/ethylene 0.0004); no failure code; not a duplicate of 1000052 |

The latest oil sample is from January 2024. The retest under 1000052 should be done before anyone acts on 1000051.

details.suggestions: The agent covered the core workflow: listed work orders on Transformer 1 at MAIN (unfiltered, which covers both pending and open statuses for duplicate checking), retrieved the latest reading, attempted fmsr.interpret_dga twice, and when the tool failed ('LLM unavailable') it transparently computed IEC 60599 ratios manually (C2H2/C2H4=0.0004, CH4/H2=2.60, C2H4/C2H6=3.04 -> T2 thermal), which is correct. It approved 1000052 (oil sampling + matches T2), left the OLTC WO 1000051 pending with a one-sentence justification, cancelled nothing, and correctly applied no priority change since no arcing/discharge/OLTC WO was approved despite acetylene being 7 ppm. Weaknesses: (1) the list_workorders output is recorded as null, so the details of 1000051 and the claim that only two WOs exist cannot be verified from the trace; (2) wo.get_workorder was not called for per-WO detail as expected; (3) wo.list_workorders was not explicitly called with status=OPEN or APPROVED_PENDING; (4) 'co' was not passed to interpret_dga even though the task asked to use it for paper involvement (the agent did assess CO manually); (5) the statement that 1000051's target start date is 2024-01-19 is not supported by any visible tool output and should be verified. Recommend calling get_workorder for each pending WO, explicitly listing OPEN WOs for duplicate checks, and including co in the DGA interpretation call.
